D.treatment: successive tuberculin skin test readings up to 50

O.outcome_detail: Agreement with lead-trainer readings

result.effect: Weighted Kappa 0.864 overall; first-reading agreement 88.1%; category agreement 93.0%, 74.8%, and 88.2%

cells.quote: The agreement between the trained professionals and the multipliers was 93.0% for readings between 0 mm and 4 mm, 74.8% for readings between 5 mm and 9 mm, and 88.2% for readings of 10 mm or more (Kappa weighted 0.864) (Table 2). Agreement in the first reading was 88.1%, and no variations greater than 5.0% were observed (Figure 2).
cells.note: The study reports no substantive effect across successive readings, but does not report an equivalence test or adequate power; therefore direction is coded ns.

D.treatment: successive tuberculin skin test readings up to 50

O.outcome_detail: Difference between professional and lead-trainer measurements

result.effect: Mean difference 0.01 mm (±0.70 mm) overall; 0.03 mm at the first reading

cells.quote: The mean difference between the readings of each of the 168 trained professionals and the lead trainers was 0.01 mm (±0,70). Considering only the first reading, the mean difference was 0.03 mm, and the differences remained stable throughout the readings, with no downward trend (Figure 1).
cells.note: The study reports stable differences, but does not report an equivalence test or adequate power; therefore direction is coded ns.

D.treatment: successive tuberculin skin test readings up to 50

O.outcome_detail: Sensitivity and specificity using lead trainers as the gold standard

result.effect: At 5 mm: sensitivity 96.5%, specificity 93.0%; at 10 mm: sensitivity 88.2%, specificity 95.0%; first-reading values ranged from 93.0% to 96.3%

cells.quote: Considering the 5 mm cutoff, sensitivity and specificity were 96.5% and 93.0%, respectively, with values of 93.3% and 93.8% at the first reading. The values remained high in subsequent readings, with very small variations throughout, not exceeding 5.0% (Figure 3). For the 10 mm cutoff, sensitivity and specificity were 88.2% and 95.0%, respectively, with values of 93.0% and 96.3% at the first reading, again showing no substantive effect over successive readings.
cells.note: The study reports no substantive effect, but does not report an equivalence test or adequate power; therefore direction is coded ns.
